subject: Regional availability validation, credit eligibility, and request for expedited post‑mortem
summary: Customer reports a regional availability blackout impacting checkout calls in us-west-2 on 2028-10-29. Engineering confirmed a 52-minute blackout caused by an autoscaler misconfiguration + eviction storm. Customer requests validation of the downtime window, SLA credit eligibility, and an expedited postmortem + evidence bundle for procurement to process a credit hold.
messages:
From: Sarah Patel <sarah@blueharbor-payments.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@blueharbor-payments.com
Date: Mon, 29 Oct 2028 23:06:10 -0400
Subject: sudden region outage - checkout failures (us-west-2)

Hi David,

We saw a pretty bad window this evening (us-east time) where ~30% of checkout requests returned 503s and a number of tokenized sessions failed to resume. Our SRE told us the spike lasted about an hour starting ~22:07 UTC on 2028-10-29 and briefly prevented a tranche of transactions from completing. We opened a ticket with your support portal (INF-5821) but need confirmation of the exact affected window and whether this maps to Redwood's SLA coverage for availability.

We also need the raw evidence bundle (traces, ingress logs) to present to procurement — they are asking for a formal statement we can attach to a credit request. Can you confirm ASAP whether BlueHarbor is eligible for a service credit and when we can expect your postmortem?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sr. Ops Manager | BlueHarbor Payments
ops@blueharbor-payments.com

Attachments: none (we've included a short CSV of sample request IDs in the support ticket)

From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Patel <sarah@blueharbor-payments.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Oct 2028 02:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden region outage - checkout failures (us-west-2)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as high priority.

Quick notes / asks:
- Can you confirm the customer sample request IDs you attached to the ticket? That helps match traces.
- We'll validate the exact blackout window (ingress metrics, routing fallbacks) and return a timestamped evidence bundle.
- If the event meets the SLA definition for an Availability incident, we will outline the credit calculation and next steps.

I'll loop in Steph (serving runtime) and Marcus (SLA ops) to pull the traces and start a preliminary RCA. Sarah — target timeline: provisional window and evidence by EOD your time (Tue 30 Oct), final postmortem within 72 hours unless further data needed. If BlueHarbor needs a faster attestation for procurement, let me know and we can prioritize a compact evidence packet.

— David Kim
Account Lead, Enterprise Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, Sarah Patel <sarah@blueharbor-payments.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Oct 2028 11:42:08 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden region outage - checkout failures (us-west-2)

FYI — preliminary findings attached.

Summary (prelim):
- Verified an availability gap in us-west-2 between 2028-10-29T22:07:00Z and 2028-10-29T22:59:00Z (~52 minutes) where the primary routing plane returned elevated 503s and several autoscaler evictions coincided with a burst in ephemeral node churn.
- Root cause (prelim): misconfigured scaling policy on a controller responsible for warm pool replenishment; under load the controller reaped in-use instances leading to an eviction cascade.
- Impact: subset of checkout traffic (approx 28–33% for affected shard range) experienced timeouts and 503s; retries recovered some sessions but several requests failed client-side.

Attached evidence: blueharbor-error-snaps-20281029.zip (ingress counters, sample traces), ingest-trace-20281029.json (KV cache op timeline). We'll redact internal hostnames prior to final bundle.

SLA guidance (prelim): event looks like it meets the definition of an Availability incident under Section 3.2 of the SLA — we should prepare a compensation calculation based on the affected window and BlueHarbor's committed monthly uptime. Marcus, can you confirm the credit formula and whether any mitigation (credits cap, proration) applies?

Steph
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, Sarah Patel <sarah@blueharbor-payments.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Nov 2028 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden region outage - checkout failures (us-west-2)

Thanks for the patience — following up with confirmed calculations and next steps.

Confirmed window: 2028-10-29T22:07:00Z — 2028-10-29T22:59:00Z (52 minutes). Evidence bundle uploaded to the Drive link in this thread. We've included per-route request counts, error rates, and sample traces mapped to the sample request IDs Sarah included in INF-5821.

Credit eligibility: based on BlueHarbor's committed uptime tier in the contract (99.95% monthly uptime), the incident meets the SLA threshold for a pro-rated credit. Estimated credit: 0.75% of monthly recurring usage for the affected period (this follows Section 4.1 formula: (Downtime minutes / Month minutes) * 100% * monthly fee, then capped by contractual maximums). We'll provide a line-item calculation and the accounting note for procurement to process the hold.

Next steps:
- I'll produce a short statement (PDF) that procurement can use to initiate the credit hold — expected by 2028-11-02 EOD.
- Final postmortem (RCA, mitigation, timeline for a permanent fix to the autoscaler policy) will be published to the customer portal by 2028-11-05.
- If BlueHarbor needs a notarized evidence pack sooner for an internal audit, please reply with the procurement contact and the required format; we can prioritize.

Marcus Lin
SLA & Ops, Redwood Inference
